universal_lens: A mathematical framework for defensive positioning in baseball integrates historical batter hit distributions with spatial risk penalties to optimize fielder placement. Mathematical modeling of baseball defensive positioning distinguishes outfield circular coverage from asymmetric infield coverage zones using Euclidean distance metrics and variable lateral mobility.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs Bayesian inference to update defensive configurations using real-time batter hit probability maps derived from historical data and risk-adjusted positioning models. GSI employs Bayesian inference over spatial coverage functions to predict optimal defensive alignments; conformal prediction bounds uncertainty in player coverage scores derived from positional distances.
gse_mapping: GSE utilizes conformal prediction to dynamically transition defensive states based on evolving hit density heatmaps and risk-weighted spatial coverage metrics. GSE utilizes state-transition models to simulate real-time defensive repositioning; each player's coverage score updates dynamically based on lateral movement and proximity to home plate.
